q: What fuels do Vellore rice mill boilers burn, and what is the cluster's footprint?
title: Vellore rice mills: boiler fuels and CO2
short: Mostly firewood, then groundnut shell and rice husk, in boilers running at only 25 to 40% efficiency. All three are biogenic, so the fossil footprint of Vellore's 340 or so mills is the power bill: about 79 million kWh, roughly 53,500 t CO2 a year.
audience: Ponni rice mills in Vellore, Arcot and Arni

ul: About 340 mills: 125 below 15 t a day, 215 above.
Ponni rice leaves the mill at 8.5 to 9% moisture, against 12 to 13% in most other states.
Boilers raise steam at 1 to 2 kg per cm2 to cook paddy; hot air and bed dryers do the drying.
Energy is only 4 to 5% of the cost of processing paddy.

sections.h: The cluster's fuel in a year
ul: Electricity: about 79.3 million kWh, 6% of the energy but almost all of the fossil CO2.

p: BEE's three study mills each processed 4,950 t of paddy. One used 228,576 kWh, another 482,880. Wood ran at 0.12 to 0.13 kg per kg of paddy in all three, but groundnut shell ranged from 0.05 to 0.11. Compare your own kWh and fuel per tonne against these before buying anything.

The study found single pass, locally built boilers at 25 to 40% efficiency and recommended three pass boilers at about 72%. Across 295 mills it put the saving at 54,967 t of biomass a year, with payback under a year. Less wood also means less methane and nitrous oxide, which do count in Scope 1.

example.title: One study mill, one year (estimate)
lines: Paddy: 4,950 t; electricity 228,576 kWh; wood 660 t; groundnut shell 264 t
Electricity: 228,576 x 0.675 = 154 t CO2, or 31 kg per tonne of paddy
Methane and nitrous oxide from the wood alone: about 10.3 TJ x 1.9 t = about 20 t CO2e, in Scope 1
Wood CO2: 660 t x 1.75 = about 1,155 t, reported separately as biogenic
Cluster: 79.3 million kWh x 0.675 = about 53,500 t fossil CO2
example.note: Fuel, power and paddy from BEE's energy conservation manual for the Vellore cluster. Wood at the IPCC default heat value and factors; groundnut shell and husk add to both biogenic lines.
